# Review of iliad-125 (Iliad 19.238–337)

Two full passes. Pass 1 on the drafter's file, pass 2 on the edited file (reread every `l`, `i` and every changed note; rechecked quotation marks, `p`, `mark`, mid-line statements, `t` unchanged by script comparison, `l` line count = `t` line count). No `gloss.json` exists yet, so no parses were checked. Neighbour: iliad-124's last unit (19.236–237) closes Odysseus's speech with ” and this part opens in narration, so no speech runs in; iliad-126 does not exist, and the last unit here (Achilles, 19.335–337) closes with ”, the speech ending at 337.

Counts: high 1, medium 15, low 23 (39 findings; several touch more than one field).

## Drafter's flagged points

- 318 “spoken earlier in the poem”: certain, it is 8.516 (iliad-051, unit at 8.513–516, in Hector's speech to the Trojans, mark at 8.497). Named in the note.
- 238 “sons of Nestor”: no certain solution. Nothing in the poem names the five (Meges, Thoas, Meriones, Lycomedes, Melanippus) as Nestor's sons, and the τε after Φυλεΐδην adds them to the sons of Nestor. The note's “either … or” and “the English decides nothing” stand; `l` and `i` both keep “sons of Nestor” and the added “and”.
- 262 κεχρημένος: construction re-parsed (see 261 above); the best reading is unchanged in sense.
- 305 ἐπιπείθεθ’: 3rd singular with aspirated elision (see above); no change to `l`/`i`.
- 273 ἀμήχανος: the departure from “helpless” is justified, and in fact is not a departure but the Iliad table's own rendering of the word for persons (10.167, 13.726, 15.14, 16.29); “helpless” is the Odyssey's word and would make Achilles pity Agamemnon.

## Considered and refused

- 272 `i` “against my will”: kept; the table keeps it for plain phrases and iliad-003 (1.300) has the same `i`.
- 247 `i` “along with him” for ἅμα: kept; ἅμα + ἦρχ’ puts the others with Odysseus.
- 242 `l` “was accomplished” for the pluperfect τετέλεστο: kept; the note says “had been accomplished” and the pluperfect is a plain past in this idiom.
- 282 `l` one “then” for ἄρα and ἔπειτα: kept; the Greek particles are weak, and the table does not fix them.
- 328 note “Argos here is the Greek homeland”: kept; the note's “Greek” is descriptive, not the banned rendering of Δαναοί, and the identification is traditional.
- 290 `l`/`i` for δέχεται κακὸν ἐκ κακοῦ: kept; either noun can be the subject, and the note says the Greek does not say more.
- 317–318 `i`: kept as the published 8.516 wording.
- 311 ἱππηλάτα as nominative in -α and similar epic morphology labels in the notes (βὰν, θέσαν, μενέτην, ἦρχ’, ἔμεν’, ἐπέσπον, ἐώλπει, χυμένη): checked, true as stated.
- Scansion: the packet flags none; no line was scanned out of suspicion, no sentence about metre added.
- Quotation marks, `mark` and `p` fields: all correct (opens at 258, 270, 287, 305, 315; closes at 264, 275, 300, 308, 337 (unit ln 335); `p` at 238, 266, 276, 282, 301, 309).

Counts: medium 6, low 11 (17 changes: 11 novel entries, 6 broaden entries; of the 15 broaden entries, 3 removed, 2 amended, 1 new one added; 13 remain).

Broaden entries checked and kept: ἄν (ὡς ἄν + opt., 331), μὴ (μὴ μέν + aor. indic. oath, 261), ὑπὸ (+ acc. place where, 258), κατὰ (κατὰ πάμπαν, 334), ἐπίορκον (264), σίτοιο, ποτῆτος (object of ἄσασθαι, 305), πόσιος, ἐδητύος (gen. of lack with ἄκμηνος, 319), πολέμου (dependent on στόμα, 312); each is old entry whole + " · " + new reading, correct, and needed.

Known forms checked against their entries and found already covered (no broadening): ἂν at 249 (ἀνά in tmesis) and 271 (past unreal), κε 272, κεν 321 (εἴ κεν + opt.), τώ 300 (adverb), ἦρχ’ 247 (absolute), ἐφ’ 317 (+ dat. ’against’), ἐπ’ 255 (φιν-form), ἀπὸ 252/266, ἐς 308, ἥ 252, αὐτῶν 301, δῶρα, θεράποντες, Ἀργεῖοι and the rest.

### Findings refused

- κεχρημένος "perf. part. … masc. nom. sg." without "mid.": the entry's parse is true; kept.
- κούρητες "(= Attic κοῦροι)", τίνυνται "(= Attic τίνονται)", ὀπάσσατο, ἰχθύσιν, ἐμῇσιν: Attic equivalents acceptable; kept.
- ὤρινε "aor. or impf.": the unit note says the same; kept.
- ἐπίορκον (264) gloss ’a false oath’ for a predicate adjective: loose but not wrong; kept.
- γῆ joined with "also Γῆ" by "also" rather than " · ": the entry is not a homograph pair (one noun, common and personified); kept.
- ὅτίς, ἐπιπείθεθ, ἐώλπει, χυμένη, ἀκάχησθαι, ἀλίτηται parses: checked against 264, 305, 328, 284, 335; true as stated.
